commits.message:
fix(export-html): the host page's styles stop at the fragment too

The fragment kept its own rules off the host but not the host's off it:
a docs theme's body line-height gapped every box-drawn row, and its `a`
rules made linked runs heavier than their neighbours. `all:initial` on
the pre and `all:unset` on the anchor cut both directions at once; the
e2e now compares the fragment in a hostile host against a blank page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(export-html): an embeddable fragment; the document is that fragment in a shell (rich-docs-examples-xuu.n71)

`encodeHtmlFragment` returns one `pre` carrying its canvas and every rule
inline, anchors included, so it can sit in a page this library does not own
without restyling that page's body, pre or links. The blink keyframes, the one
thing an inline style cannot say, are `HTML_FRAGMENT_CSS`, included once by the
host page. `encodeHtml` is the fragment wrapped in a document that paints the
page in the same canvas and includes that CSS, so the two cannot draw different
pictures.

Two export-html tests pinned the bare `<pre>` and `<a href>` tags; they now
match the attributed tags, their assertions otherwise unchanged.

fix(viewport): the demo paints its first frame on start (rich-viewport-owi.3)

Live.start draws nothing with autoRefresh off, so frame 0 was never shown and
the screen stayed blank until the first tick.
chore(viewport): just recipe for the viewport demo (rich-viewport-owi.3)

fix(viewport): ensureVisible counts rendered lines, and the demo follows the terminal's size (rich-viewport-owi.3)

The docs and demo passed an item index where ensureVisible counts the lines
the content renders to; the demo now renders each entry on one line and the
page says so. The demo's Console reads the host's live size and its node
bootstrap tears down on SIGTERM too. Render slices only the rows it shows.

feat(viewport): a Viewport shows a window of rows onto taller content and keeps a range in view (rich-viewport-owi.3)

Scroll operations are queued and resolved at the next render, in call order,
clamping after each move: the rows and the content's length that an offset is
clamped against only exist once the viewport renders. The scroll position
belongs to the viewport, so a view rebuilt every frame keeps one Viewport and
replaces its content.

test(docs): bundle-program reads REPO_ROOT from its one definition

test/coverage/extract.ts already owns the repository root; a second
computation from a different directory could drift from it silently.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
test(docs): overlapping runs stay in their own terminals; header names the one ambient read (rich-docs-examples-xuu.iy5)
fix(docs): runInTerminal rejects on every failure, types to ConsoleStream, bundles keep process.env (rich-docs-examples-xuu.iy5)

feat(docs): a simulated process runs an example's own new Console() in a terminal we supply (rich-docs-examples-xuu.iy5)

`runInTerminal(program, terminal)` evaluates a bundled program as the body of
an async function whose parameter is named `process`, so every free `process`
in it — the library included — binds to a stand-in built from the terminal.
Nothing global is swapped: the build's and the page's own `process` are never
touched, and two runs can overlap.

Proven in Node (test/docs/simulated-process.test.ts, under a hostile host env)
and in Chromium (e2e/simulated-process.spec.ts).

docs: TERM=dumb drops hyperlinks; console.destination in the attributes table (#167)
